echo $$.description: PSH and bash report different process IDs ($$) because they are distinct processes

expected.note: Both print their OWN pid: same shape, different value.

echo \\$(echo test).description: Both shells reject backslash-escaped $( as syntax error with exit code 2. Error message format differs.
echo \\$(echo test).psh_behavior: Syntax error with PSH error format
echo \\$(echo test).bash_behavior: Syntax error with bash error format

expected.note: Same rejection and same diagnostic text; only the surrounding message FORMAT differs (psh adds a caret/context block).

alias ll=\"echo ALIAS_EXPANDED\"; ll.description: PSH deliberately keeps the expand_aliases shopt option ON in every mode (educational choice, single lex->parse alias gate in shell.py); bash defaults it OFF in non-interactive shells. Documented in user guide ch17 (17.3 Alias Expansion in Scripts) and ch04.
alias ll=\"echo ALIAS_EXPANDED\"; ll.psh_behavior: Alias expands in scripts and -c strings; prints ALIAS_EXPANDED, exit 0
alias ll=\"echo ALIAS_EXPANDED\"; ll.bash_behavior: expand_aliases is off non-interactively (and the line was read before the alias existed); ll: command not found, exit 127

expected.note: Deliberate psh divergence (expand_aliases always on). If psh ever stopped expanding, this shape stops matching and the case is no longer documented.
